title: Chapter 10 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of Docker Swarm, services, stacks, networking, secrets, and orchestration concepts!

questions.question: What is Docker Swarm mode?
options: Docker's native clustering and orchestration solution
questions.explanation: Swarm mode turns a group of Docker engines into a single, managed cluster.

questions.question: Which node type schedules tasks in a Swarm?
questions.explanation: Manager nodes handle orchestration and scheduling. Workers simply run tasks.

questions.question: A worker node can also act as a manager if needed.
questions.explanation: You can promote a worker to manager. By default, nodes are workers; managers are manually promoted.

questions.question: What command initializes a new Swarm on a node?
questions.explanation: `docker swarm init` turns the current Docker engine into a manager.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `--replicas` flag in `docker service create`?
options: Sets the number of manager nodes
Defines how many copies of the service should run
Limits the memory of each replica
questions.explanation: Replicas determine how many container instances (tasks) of that service are running.

questions.question: The Docker Swarm routing mesh ensures that only nodes running a replica can receive traffic on the published port.
questions.explanation: The routing mesh makes every node listen on the published port, and forwards traffic to a node running a replica.

questions.question: How do you scale a service named `api` to 5 replicas?
options: Both a and b are valid
questions.explanation: Both `docker service scale api=5` and `docker service update --replicas=5 api` work.

questions.question: What is a rolling update in Swarm?
options: Stopping all replicas and restarting them
Updating replicas one by one to avoid downtime
Moving the service to another node
questions.explanation: Swarm replaces one replica at a time with the new version, maintaining availability.

questions.question: To view all tasks (containers) of a service named `web`, use `docker service ___ web`.
questions.explanation: `docker service ps <service>` shows the tasks of that service and their status.

questions.question: Which command deploys a stack defined in `docker-compose.yml`?
questions.explanation: `docker stack deploy` is used to deploy Compose files in Swarm mode.

questions.question: What happens to `build` instructions in a Compose file when used with `docker stack deploy`?
options: They are ignored; images must already exist in a registry
They are executed on the manager node
questions.explanation: Swarm does not build images. You must push built images to a registry accessible by all nodes.

questions.question: What network driver allows containers on different Swarm nodes to communicate transparently?
questions.explanation: Overlay networks span multiple hosts and provide multi‑host connectivity.

questions.question: By default, communication on Swarm overlay networks is unencrypted.
questions.explanation: Swarm overlay networks encrypt data plane traffic using AES‑GCM by default.

questions.question: Where are Docker secrets mounted inside containers?
questions.explanation: Secrets appear as files under `/run/secrets/<secret_name>`.

questions.question: Which command creates a secret named `db_pass` from a file?
questions.explanation: `docker secret create <name> <file>` reads the file content. Use `-` to read from stdin.

questions.question: What is the difference between a config and a secret in Swarm?
options: Configs are encrypted; secrets are plain‑text
Secrets are encrypted; configs are plain‑text
Secrets cannot be used with stacks
questions.explanation: Secrets are for sensitive data and are encrypted. Configs are for non‑sensitive config files.

questions.question: You want to take a node offline for maintenance without disrupting running services. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Draining a node causes its tasks to be rescheduled to other nodes, allowing safe maintenance.

questions.question: A manager node cannot also run service tasks.
questions.explanation: By default, managers can run tasks. In production, you may want to set `--availability drain` on managers to keep them only for orchestration.

questions.question: How do you list all nodes in a Swarm?
questions.explanation: `docker node ls` shows the status of every node in the swarm.

questions.question: Which command would you use to see the logs of all replicas of a service?
questions.explanation: `docker service logs` aggregates logs from all replicas of a service.
